message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. Pebble Spring spent many months observing the mortar mixing, the careful stacking of stones, and the precise alignment of beams. The Leshy found that their natural affinity for wood made the framing process almost effortless. They could sense the grain of each timber and knew exactly where it would bear the most weight. The mortar work, however, proved to be a completely different challenge. Their paws were not designed for holding trowels steady or spreading thin layers of wet paste. Pebble Spring watched the human builders with intense focus, trying to memorize every movement. The rhythm of the work, the way they tapped the stones into place with a wooden mallet, all of it was fascinating. Slowly, the Leshy began to develop their own technique for mixing and applying mortar. They discovered that a small amount of water magic could help the mixture cure faster. The first wall they built was crooked and uneven, barely standing on its own. But Pebble Spring was not discouraged by the failure. They tore it down and started again the very next morning. The second wall was better, though still far from the standard the human builders expected. Pebble Spring continued to practice day after day, refining their method with each attempt. The third wall was decent enough that a human builder might have nodded in approval. By the fifth wall, the Leshy had developed a style that was distinctly their own. The stones were set with a natural, organic quality that no human builder could replicate. The mortar lines followed the same flowing patterns as the veins in a leaf. Word spread through the settlement that the Leshy was learning their craft with remarkable speed. Their progress, while remarkable in many respects and widely admired by the entire community of builders and architects who had patiently observed the Leshy work day after day for many long months, was still spotty in terms of overall consistency and reliability.
